newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two Mexican trains collide, injuring 70.
newsitem.headline: Two Mexican trains collide, injuring 70.

text.p: A Mexican passenger train crashed head on into a cargo train on Monday, injuring 70 people, 17 of them with broken bones, officials said.

Authorities said more injuries were avoided only because the passenger train was moving slowly, having just left the station in Zacoalco de Torres, about 40 miles (60 km) south of Guadalajara, Mexico's second city.

"The impact was powerful, and because we live only a few metres from the the crash, several neighbours ran to help and bring our trucks to help the injured," witness Santiago Lugo told Reuters by telephone.

Officials with the Zacoalco de Torres city hall said there were 170 passengers aboard the train that left from the port city of Manzanillo. The cargo train was arriving in Zacoalco de Torres from Guadalajara.
Both trains belonged to the state-owned rail company Ferrocarriles Nacionales. A spokesman there said there would be no comment pending an investigation.

"Of the 52 that were transported by the Red Cross ... three were diagnosed with cranial factures and (five) with neck fractures," Maria Huizar, chief social worker for the local Red Cross, told Reuters.
"Even though they were grave, they were in stable condition when they left the Red Cross and we don't think their lives are in danger," Huizar said.
